# Polymorphic -- Agent API

> Polymorphic is a free live-coding environment for shaders, built on the
> Noisemaker engine. A Polymorphic program is Noisemaker DSL text that
> compiles to a render graph. An agent can join the person's own open
> Polymorphic over Seance, the Noise Factor collaboration service, and read
> and run programs in it, look at its canvas, use the gallery, the output
> surfaces and the tempo, and move programs to other Noise Factor apps. An
> agent that drives its own browser can use the in-page
> `window.PolymorphicAgent` API instead, which also reaches that browser's
> saved programs, scenes and view. This file is the contract for software
> agents that control Polymorphic.

The full contract adds a reference for every command and its arguments:
https://polymorphic.noisedeck.app/llms-full.txt

The DSL itself (syntax, effects, parameters, surfaces) is specified by the
Noisemaker contract: https://noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt

The same agent tool controls Noisedeck, Visualize and HD4. Their contracts:
https://noisedeck.app/llms-full.txt, https://visualize.noisedeck.app/llms.txt,
https://hd4.noisefactor.io/llms.txt

## Connect to the person's Polymorphic

Use this route when you can run shell commands. It works with the Polymorphic
the person already has open: their program and their canvas.

1. Ask the person to open https://polymorphic.noisedeck.app, choose
   **connect agent...** at the end of the program menu, click **Go Online**,
   then **Copy Prompt**, and paste the prompt to you. The prompt names this
   file and the session link. (Without that dialog: **go online...**,
   **Take Online**, then send the link from **Copy URL** or the six-character
   code.)
2. Get the agent tool. It needs Node 22.4 or later and nothing else:
   `curl -fsSLO https://noisedeck.app/agent/seance-agent.mjs`
3. Join: `node seance-agent.mjs join <link-or-code>`. It prints the session
   name (`polymorphic`), the open app tabs and the program documents. A
   background process keeps the session joined between commands.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node seance-agent.mjs commands` | Lists the app's commands and their arguments. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs program [--json]` | Prints the session's program text (`--json` adds its `rev`). |
| `node seance-agent.mjs validate <file>` | Checks a program (`-` reads standard input). |
| `node seance-agent.mjs set <file>` | Runs a program in the person's tab (setProgram). |
| `node seance-agent.mjs look [--size N] [--format png\|jpg] [--out FILE]` | Saves an image of the person's canvas. Prints its path. Open the file with your image tool. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs call <command> [JSON]` | Runs any command, for example `call loadExample '{"title":"RGB Static"}'`. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs wait [--since REV] [--timeout S]` | Waits for the person to change the program, then prints it. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs image-put <file>` | Adds a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP file to the session. Prints `image:<id>`. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs image-get <id> [--out FILE]` | Saves an image of the session to a file. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs transfer <from> <to>` | Copies the program and its images from one joined session to another. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs leave` / `stop` | Leaves the session / stops the background process. |

Every command prints JSON, except `program` and `commands`, which print text
(`--json` gives JSON). The tool leaves `state` out of envelopes; `--state`
keeps it. The exit code is 0 for success, 1 when the app refused the command
(read `result.envelope.error.code`), and 2 when the tool could not run it
(read `error.code`; the codes are listed below).
`node seance-agent.mjs help` lists every option.

How it works, so you can explain it to the person:

- The tool joins the session as an anonymous participant, which the person
  sees join. It runs commands in the tab that took the program online, through
  the session, with the same checks as the person's own edits. A program that
  you run replaces the one in their editor and runs on their canvas. No other tab answers,
  even one that becomes the session's owner after the person's tab leaves.
- Everyone in the session receives every answer, and anyone who can edit the
  session can send commands to that tab. So a session reaches only the shared
  program and what is on the canvas. What the person keeps in their browser is
  not reachable: saved programs (`listPrograms`, `saveProgram`, `loadProgram`,
  `deleteProgram`), scenes (`listScenes`, `saveScene`, `loadScene`), the
  program history (`stepHistory`, `resetProgram`) and custom `user` effects
  answer `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` or are left out. A program that you run can name
  only images that are in the session (`image-put`), never one that the person
  keeps only in their browser (`NOT_FOUND_IMAGE`). `importComposition` cannot
  run through a session either: a sharing link's custom effects bring shader
  code that only the person may let in.
- Commands that act on the person's browser rather than the shared program
  answer `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` too: downloads (`exportImage`, `setRecording`),
  `setFullscreen`, `useLiveInput`, the panels (`setView`) and the renderer
  (`setBackend`). `commands` marks all of them "not available remotely".
- While the person uses live camera, screen or video input, that input stays in
  their browser: every command answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` until they stop it.
  `getProgram` returns the program that the session holds.
- The person can change the program at the same time. Read it again before
  you edit it. `wait --since <rev>` returns at once when the person changed the
  program after that revision.
- `look` asks the person's tab for an image of the canvas: the frame on the
  screen, which a paused animation keeps. The tab adds the image to the session
  as its own bytes, and the tool saves it as a file. Do not print image bytes as
  text. No image crosses a session as text (`IMAGE_AS_TEXT`).
- A session holds at most 32 images, and the person's own images need room
  too. The tab takes at most 16 images in ten minutes; past that, `look`
  answers `IMAGE_LIMIT` with `details.retryAfter` in seconds. Look when the
  program has changed, not in a loop.
- Suggest that the person goes offline (**Go Offline** in the same dialog)
  when you are done.

Work with several apps at once: join each app's session (each gets its own
name, such as `polymorphic`, `noisedeck` or `visualize`), then name the session
in each command: `set polymorphic prog.dsl`, `look noisedeck`,
`transfer polymorphic noisedeck`. A transfer copies the program's images as
bytes, so `media(url: "image:<sha256>")` references keep working. The target
app checks the program and refuses one that it cannot compile.

Agent tool errors (exit code 2, `error.code`):

- `NO_SESSION`: no session is joined, or more than one and none was named.
- `UNKNOWN_SESSION`, `SESSION_LOCKED`, `REFUSED`: the session code is wrong or
  expired, the session is locked, or the session refused the join.
- `NO_APP_TAB`: the tab that took the session online did not answer. Ask the
  person to keep it open, or to go online again and send the new code.
- `TIMEOUT`: the tab did not answer in time. Check `status`, then try again.
- `READONLY`: the session lets this agent only read.
- `SESSION_CLOSED`, `SESSION_REFUSED`: the connection closed, or the session
  server refused a request (the message says why).
- `IMAGE_FAILED`, `NO_DOCUMENT`, `USAGE`, `INVALID_JSON`: an image transfer
  failed, a document is missing, or the command line was wrong.

## Control Polymorphic in a browser you drive

Use this route when you control a browser yourself. Open
https://polymorphic.noisedeck.app. This is a Polymorphic of its own, not the
person's tab: its saved programs and scenes are those of that browser.
Use the first route your browser tool supports:

1. WebMCP: discover the page tools named `polymorphic_getState`,
   `polymorphic_setProgram`, and so on. Each tool has the argument schema in
   the command reference. These call the same API and return its envelope as
   text. `getThumbnail` also returns an image content block, without
   duplicating its bytes in text. If your harness serializes the whole tool
   result, parse it, display the image through your image tool, and print only
   the text block. Do not print image bytes.
2. Page JavaScript: call `window.PolymorphicAgent` directly. Wait until the
   object and method exist. Every command waits for startup automatically;
   explicitly awaiting `ready` also works. Return the fields you need, not the
   whole API object.

```js
const env = await window.PolymorphicAgent.getProgram()
return env.result.dsl
```

Both routes use the same serialized commands and validation. WebMCP
availability depends on the browser. If discovery returns no tools, use page
JavaScript. Do not try to bypass a browser tool's read-only JavaScript
policy. A tool that only fetches HTML cannot run Polymorphic: it needs a
browser with WebGL2 or WebGPU.

---

## Write a program

1. Find effects with `searchEffects`. Read their parameters with `getEffectDefinition`.
2. Write the program. Copy each parameter name from `getEffectDefinition`. Do not guess names.
   `choices` lists accepted values. For a `member` parameter, insert its value as a DSL
   member expression, such as `palette.hypercolor`, without quotes.
3. Check it with `validateProgram`. Fix every diagnostic with severity `error`.
4. Run it with `setProgram`. Look at the result with `getThumbnail` (`look` in a session).
5. To start from an existing program, use `listExamples` and `loadExample`. In
   a browser you drive, `importComposition` loads a sharing link and
   `saveProgram` keeps the result in the saved programs; through a session, ask
   the person to do these from the program menu ("import from url...",
   "save program").

```js
const A = window.PolymorphicAgent
const dsl = [
    'search synth, filter',
    'perlin(scale: 75, octaves: 2)',
    '  .adjust(mode: hsv, rotation: 120, hueRange: 40)',
    '  .write(o0)',
    'render(o0)',
].join('\n')
const check = await A.validateProgram({ dsl })
if (!check.result.valid) return check.result.diagnostics
const run = await A.setProgram({ dsl })
return { ok: run.ok, error: run.error }
```

DSL rules that agents most often get wrong:

- The first line `search ns1, ns2` sets the namespaces that effect names resolve in, in order.
  The same function name can mean different effects: `noise` is `synth/noise` under
  `search synth` and `classicNoisedeck/noise` under `search classicNoisedeck`.
  The two take different parameters.
- Every chain ends with `.write(oN)`. The program ends with `render(oN)`.
- Read another surface with `read(oN)`, for example `tex: read(o0)`.
- Noisemaker retired all old parameter aliases. Older examples use names
  such as `mixAmt`, `noiseType` or `loopAmp`. Those now fail with
  `S001 Unknown argument`. `getEffectDefinition` gives the current names.

What Polymorphic adds to the DSL:

- `media(url: "image:<sha256>")` shows an image. The id is the SHA-256 of the
  image file's bytes. In a session, add the file with `image-put` first and use
  the `image:<id>` that it prints. Saved programs and scenes keep their images
  in the browser. Use only image ids: a link to another site makes every
  viewer's browser fetch it, and a session refuses one (`OUTSIDE_LINK`).
- `media()` draws the image at its own size in pixels, in the middle of the
  canvas. `scaleAmt`, `position` and `tiling` change that; read them with
  `getEffectDefinition({ effectId: "synth/media" })`.
- `media()` without `url` shows the live source that the person started:
  the webcam, a screen capture or a video file.
- `text(text: "Hello", font: "Nunito", size: 0.1)` (effect `filter/text`) draws
  text over its input. The browser draws the words, in fonts from
  https://fonts.noisefactor.io. Read the other parameters with
  `getEffectDefinition({ effectId: "filter/text" })`.
- Custom effects, from a sharing link (`importComposition`) or a ZIP that the
  person imported, are in the `user` namespace. Add `user` to the search line,
  for example `search user, synth`. In a browser you drive,
  `searchEffects({ namespace: "user" })` lists them; a session does not show them.
- With the microphone on, a parameter can follow the sound:
  `audio(band: low, min: 0, max: 1)`, with band `low`, `mid`, `high` or `vol`.
  With MIDI on, `midi(channel: 1, controller: 7, min: 0, max: 1)` follows a controller.
- One animation loop lasts one bar of the tempo (`setTempo`).

Every command that changes the program checks it first. A program with an
`error` diagnostic changes nothing. A program that runs goes to the online
session, the program history (`stepHistory`) and the page URL, as typing it
would.

---

## Keep results small

Your tools send each result back to you. A large result uses a large part of
your context.

- Return only the fields that you need from each script.
- Every envelope includes `state`. Remove it when you do not need it.
- `getProgram` returns the whole program text. `state.program.chars` gives its length.
- Direct JavaScript `getThumbnail` returns base64 image data. Keep `maxDimension` small.
  WebMCP and `look` keep image bytes out of text.

---

## The envelope

Every command response, success or failure, has this shape:

```js
// success
{ ok: true, command: "setProgram", apiVersion: "1.0", result: { /* command-specific */ }, state: { /* snapshot */ } }

// failure
{
    ok: false,
    command: "setProgram",
    apiVersion: "1.0",
    error: { code: "INVALID_PROGRAM", message: "...", details: { diagnostics: [ /* ... */ ] } },
    state: { /* snapshot */ }
}
```

Commands run one at a time, in the order you call them.
You can omit the argument object: `getState()` is the same as `getState({})`.
Every command rejects an argument that it does not declare, so a command
with no arguments accepts only `{}`.

---

## State snapshot

```
state: {
    schemaVersion,
    program:  { chars, running, error },  // running: the editor text is the program that runs
                                          // error: the compiler error on screen, or null
                                          // through a session: the text that the session holds
    canvas:   { width, height },
    output:   { surface, written },       // surface: "o0" to "o7", the surface on the canvas
                                          // written: the surfaces that the program writes
    playback: { playing },
    tempo:    { bpm, divider, source },   // source: "manual" or "midi"
    backend,                              // "webgl2" or "webgpu"
    history:  { canBack, canForward },    // stepHistory; null through a session
    online,                               // "offline", "connecting", "online" or "readonly"
    recording,                            // a video recording is running
    liveMedia,                            // a webcam, screen capture or video is the media() source
    view:     { editor, docs, liveInputs, surfacePips, performanceOverlay, statusRow, performanceMode }
}
```

---

## Diagnostics

`validateProgram` and a refused program return compiler diagnostics:

```js
{ code: "S001", severity: "error", message: "Unknown argument 'mixAmt' for blendMode()", location?: { line, column } }
```

A syntax error has code `SYNTAX`. Diagnostics with severity `warning` do not stop a program.

---

## Error codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_ARGS_TYPE` | wrong argument type |
| `INVALID_ARGS_REQUIRED` | missing required argument |
| `INVALID_ARGS_RANGE` | number or string length out of range, or a blank name |
| `INVALID_ARGS_ENUM` | value not in the allowed list |
| `INVALID_ARGS_UNKNOWN` | an argument that the command does not declare |
| `INVALID_PROGRAM` | the program does not compile, or the editor is empty. `details.diagnostics` lists the errors. Nothing changed |
| `COMPILE_FAILED` | the renderer rejected a program that passed the compiler. The previous program runs again |
| `CONFLICT_PROGRAM_CHANGED` | the program changed while the command ran, for example because the person typed. Read it again and retry |
| `CONFLICT_PROGRAM_EXISTS` | `saveProgram` with a name in use and no `overwrite` |
| `CONFLICT_TEMPO_SOURCE` | `setTempo` with `bpm` while the tempo follows MIDI clock |
| `NOT_FOUND_EFFECT` | unknown effect id |
| `NOT_FOUND_EXAMPLE` | no gallery example has that title |
| `NOT_FOUND_PROGRAM` | no saved program has that name |
| `NOT_FOUND_SCENE` | the scene slot is empty |
| `NOT_FOUND_COMMAND` | no command has that name |
| `EFFECT_LOAD_FAILED` | an effect could not load from the CDN |
| `IMPORT_FAILED` | the sharing link is not valid, or its composition could not load |
| `STORAGE_FAILED` | browser storage refused a save or a delete. `details.quotaExceeded` tells whether it is full |
| `BROWSER_REFUSED` | the browser refused fullscreen or a recording |
| `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` | the command came through a session, and it needs the person at the browser or reaches what they keep in this browser; or the person is using live camera, screen or video input, and nothing reaches the session |
| `NOT_FOUND_IMAGE` | through a session, the program names an `image:<sha256>` that is not in the session. Add it with `image-put` |
| `IMAGE_LIMIT` | the tab already took 16 images in ten minutes. `details.retryAfter` is in seconds |
| `IMAGE_AS_TEXT` | a session request or answer would carry an image as base64 text. Add the image with `image-put` and use `image:<sha256>` |
| `OUTSIDE_LINK` | a session request names media by an outside link. Add the image with `image-put` and use `image:<sha256>` |
| `IMAGE_UPLOAD_FAILED` | the tab could not add an image to the session (the session holds up to 32 images) |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | unexpected failure |

---

  (command descriptions)

## Command reference

Polymorphic has 31 commands. In the page, call a command as `await window.PolymorphicAgent.<name>(args)`.
Through a Seance session, run it with `node seance-agent.mjs call <name> '<JSON args>'`.
Every command rejects an argument that it does not declare, with `INVALID_ARGS_UNKNOWN`.

### Read state

#### `getState`

Returns the state snapshot. Every envelope already includes it in `state`.

Returns: the snapshot.

Arguments: none.

#### `getProgram`

Returns the program text in the editor, and whether it is the program that runs. Through a Seance session it returns the text that the session holds.

Returns: `{ dsl, running }`.

Arguments: none.

### Programs

#### `validateProgram`

Compiles `dsl` without applying it.

Returns: `{ valid, diagnostics }`.

Arguments:

- `dsl` (required): string, at least 1 character

#### `setProgram`

Puts `dsl` in the editor and runs it, like typing it. The program is checked first: one that does not compile changes nothing (INVALID_PROGRAM). If the renderer rejects it, the previous program runs again (COMPILE_FAILED). While the animation plays, the command returns once the new program has drawn a frame. A program that runs goes to the online session, the program history and the page URL. Through a session, every `image:<sha256>` that the program names must already be in the session (NOT_FOUND_IMAGE).

Returns: `{ applied: true, diagnostics }` (warnings only).

Arguments:

- `dsl` (required): string, at least 1 character

#### `formatProgram`

Formats the program in the editor, like the "Format DSL" action, and runs the result. A program that does not compile stays as it is (INVALID_PROGRAM).

Returns: `{ changed }`, false when the program was already formatted.

Arguments: none.

#### `resetProgram`

Runs the original program again: the program loaded at startup, or the last gallery example loaded. The program is checked first: one that does not compile changes nothing (INVALID_PROGRAM). If the renderer rejects it, the previous program runs again (COMPILE_FAILED). While the animation plays, the command returns once the new program has drawn a frame.

Returns: `{ applied: true, diagnostics }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments: none.

#### `stepHistory`

Steps through the history of programs that ran, like Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Left and Right. `back` runs the older program, `forward` the newer one. The history is stored in the browser, so a session cannot reach it.

Returns: `{ applied }`, false when there is no older or newer program.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `direction` (required): string, one of `back`, `forward`

### Gallery and shared links

#### `listExamples`

Lists the examples in the gallery, without their program text.

Returns: `{ total, examples: [{ title, tagline, tags }] }`.

Arguments: none.

#### `loadExample`

Runs the gallery example named `title`. Without `title` it runs a random example, like "Shuffle to a random example". The example becomes the program that resetProgram restores. The program is checked first: one that does not compile changes nothing (INVALID_PROGRAM). If the renderer rejects it, the previous program runs again (COMPILE_FAILED). While the animation plays, the command returns once the new program has drawn a frame.

Returns: `{ title, applied: true, diagnostics }`.

Arguments:

- `title`: string, at least 1 character

#### `importComposition`

Loads a composition from a Noise Factor sharing link (https://sharing.noisedeck.app/s/CODE) or its code, like "import from url...". Custom effects in the composition join the `user` namespace. A session cannot load one: a custom effect brings its own shader code, which only the person may let into their tab. The program is checked first: one that does not compile changes nothing (INVALID_PROGRAM). If the renderer rejects it, the previous program runs again (COMPILE_FAILED). While the animation plays, the command returns once the new program has drawn a frame.

Returns: `{ title, effects, images, applied: true, diagnostics }`, where `effects` lists the custom effect names and `images` counts the images.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `link` (required): string, at least 1 character

### Saved programs

#### `listPrograms`

Lists the programs saved in this browser.

Returns: `{ total, programs: [{ name, savedAt, chars }] }`, with `savedAt` in milliseconds since 1970.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments: none.

#### `saveProgram`

Saves the program in the editor under `name`, with its images, like "save program". A name that is in use fails with CONFLICT_PROGRAM_EXISTS unless `overwrite` is true.

Returns: `{ saved: true, name }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `name` (required): string, at least 1 character
- `overwrite`: boolean, default `false`

#### `loadProgram`

Runs the saved program named `name`, like "load program". The program is checked first: one that does not compile changes nothing (INVALID_PROGRAM). If the renderer rejects it, the previous program runs again (COMPILE_FAILED). While the animation plays, the command returns once the new program has drawn a frame.

Returns: `{ name, applied: true, diagnostics }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `name` (required): string, at least 1 character

#### `deleteProgram`

Deletes the saved program named `name`, like "delete program". This cannot be undone.

Returns: `{ deleted: true, name }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `name` (required): string, at least 1 character

### Scenes

#### `listScenes`

Lists the scene slots that hold a program. Scenes are slots 1 to 9 that the number keys recall, stored in the browser.

Returns: `{ scenes: [{ slot, chars }] }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments: none.

#### `saveScene`

Saves the program in the editor, with its images, to scene `slot`, like Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+1 to 9.

Returns: `{ saved: true, slot }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `slot` (required): integer, from 1 to 9

#### `loadScene`

Runs the program in scene `slot`, like the number keys 1 to 9. The program is checked first: one that does not compile changes nothing (INVALID_PROGRAM). If the renderer rejects it, the previous program runs again (COMPILE_FAILED). While the animation plays, the command returns once the new program has drawn a frame.

Returns: `{ slot, applied: true, diagnostics }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `slot` (required): integer, from 1 to 9

### Effects

#### `searchEffects`

Lists effects whose id, description or tags contain `query`. `namespace` keeps one namespace. Custom effects are in the `user` namespace; a session lists only the built-in effects.

Returns: `{ total, effects: [{ effectId, namespace, name, description, tags }] }`.

Arguments:

- `query`: string
- `namespace`: string
- `limit`: integer, from 1 to 500, default `50`

#### `getEffectDefinition`

Returns the DSL function name and the parameters of one effect. Through a session, a custom (`user`) effect answers REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE.

Returns: `{ effectId, func, namespace, description, params: [{ name, type, default, min?, max?, enum?, choices?, label? }] }`.

Arguments:

- `effectId` (required): string, at least 1 character

### Output surfaces

#### `setOutput`

Shows surface `surface` on the canvas by changing the program's `render(oN)` line, like "Switch render output". `next` and `previous` move through the surfaces that the program writes. The program is checked first: one that does not compile changes nothing (INVALID_PROGRAM). If the renderer rejects it, the previous program runs again (COMPILE_FAILED). While the animation plays, the command returns once the new program has drawn a frame.

Returns: `{ surface, changed }`.

Arguments:

- `surface` (required): string, one of `o0`, `o1`, `o2`, `o3`, `o4`, `o5`, `o6`, `o7`, `next`, `previous`

#### `clearSurfaces`

Clears the feedback state of surfaces o0 to o7 by compiling the program again, like "Hush".

Returns: `{ cleared: true }`.

Arguments: none.

### Playback and tempo

#### `play`

Starts the animation.

Returns: `{ playing }`.

Arguments: none.

#### `pause`

Stops the animation. The current frame stays visible.

Returns: `{ playing }`.

Arguments: none.

#### `setTempo`

Sets the tempo. One animation loop lasts one bar of four beats, times `divider`. Omit a field to keep its value. While the tempo follows MIDI clock, `bpm` fails with CONFLICT_TEMPO_SOURCE.

Returns: `{ bpm, divider, source, loopSeconds }`, where `source` is `manual` or `midi`.

Arguments:

- `bpm`: number, from 20 to 400
- `divider`: integer, one of `1`, `2`, `4`, `8`, `16`, `32`

### View

#### `setView`

Shows or hides a panel: the code editor, the documentation, the live inputs panel, the surface previews (`surfacePips`), the performance overlay or the status row. `performanceMode` hides everything but the canvas.

Returns: `{ panel, visible }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `panel` (required): string, one of `editor`, `docs`, `liveInputs`, `surfacePips`, `performanceOverlay`, `statusRow`, `performanceMode`
- `visible` (required): boolean

#### `setBackend`

Selects the WebGL2 or WebGPU renderer and reloads the page, like the "Switch to ... backend" actions. A browser without WebGPU stays on WebGL2.

Returns: `{ backend, reloading }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `backend` (required): string, one of `webgl2`, `webgpu`

### Images

#### `getThumbnail`

Returns an image of the frame on the canvas. Nothing renders for it: while the animation is paused, the image is the frame on screen, which can be from before the last program change. Through a Seance session the image is added to the session as its own bytes, and `image` replaces `bytes`.

Returns: `{ bytes, mimeType, width, height }`, with `bytes` in base64. Through a session: `{ image: { id, mimeType, bytes }, mimeType, width, height }`, where `image.bytes` is the byte count.

Arguments:

- `maxDimension`: integer, from 16 to 1024, default `256`
- `format`: string, one of `png`, `jpg`, default `jpg`

#### `exportImage`

Saves the canvas as a browser download, like "quick save as png" and "quick save as jpg". Observe the browser download to confirm the file.

Returns: `{ started: true, format, width, height }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `format`: string, one of `png`, `jpg`, default `png`

### At the browser

#### `setRecording`

Starts or stops a video recording of the canvas. Stopping it starts a browser download of the video. `quality` selects `high` (1080p), `standard` (720p) or `low` (480p) for the next recording.

Returns: `{ recording, quality }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `recording` (required): boolean
- `quality`: string, one of `high`, `standard`, `low`

#### `setFullscreen`

Enters or leaves fullscreen. The browser allows fullscreen only soon after the person clicked or pressed a key; otherwise this fails with BROWSER_REFUSED.

Returns: `{ fullscreen }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `fullscreen` (required): boolean

#### `useLiveInput`

Opens the live inputs panel and starts a source, like the command palette actions: the webcam or a screen capture as the media() source, the microphone for audio values, or MIDI. The browser asks the person for permission. This returns before the person answers; read `state.liveMedia` later.

Returns: `{ requested: true, source }`.

Not available through a Seance session (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Arguments:

- `source` (required): string, one of `webcam`, `screen`, `microphone`, `midi`
